scenarios.title: New posts and favorites do not shift old pages
scenarios.description: Viewer V follows ordinary author A and pull author B. The v1 ranking is deterministic; refreshing starts a different session.

steps.title: Merge overlap once and freeze the order
steps.note: Pushed references overlap B's pull timeline at p3. The snapshot contains each ID once; page one returns p5 and p4.

steps.title: p6 arrives after session creation
steps.note: The authoritative post and pull timeline now contain p6, but the existing session's order and cursor position are unchanged.

steps.title: Continue the original session
steps.note: The original cursor returns p3 and p2. A changing global offset would have moved underneath the reader; this snapshot does not.

steps.title: Refresh chooses a new candidate snapshot
steps.note: Refresh is a new traversal. It can include p6 and repeat p5 intentionally; response/session identities remain distinct.

steps.title: A favorite changes only a new ranking
steps.note: The defined 30-minute favorite boost places A's p4 and p2 first. Earlier snapshots keep their already-frozen order.

scenarios.title: A stored reference does not grant permission
scenarios.description: Use page size1 and scan budget2 to see why the cursor tracks examined candidates, including newly hidden ones.

steps.title: Page one returns p5
steps.note: The session retains p5,p4,p3,p2,p1. It freezes order, not permanent permission.

steps.title: p4 becomes author-only; p3 is deleted
steps.note: Old references and session IDs remain, but they are not permission to expose either body.

steps.title: A filtered empty page still advances
steps.note: The budget scans p4 and p3, filters both, and advances to index3. The continuation is not null, so this empty page does not mean exhaustion.

steps.title: Unfollow changes the next gate
steps.note: p2 and p1 remain materialized candidates but no longer belong to this home feed.

steps.title: The final hidden candidates are consumed
steps.note: The cursor advances to index5 and becomes null. No private/deleted/unfollowed body was returned by these pages.

scenarios.title: A cursor has an owner and a lifetime
scenarios.description: Authentication and session retention are separate from ranking. Capacity eviction also produces refresh-required, rather than silent continuation.

steps.title: The cursor belongs to V and this session
steps.note: The signed cursor authenticates the viewer, session position and local instance. It is not just a base64 index.

steps.title: A different viewer cannot reuse it
steps.note: No page content is returned to the other viewer and V's legitimate cursor is not consumed.

steps.title: At five minutes, expiry is exact
steps.note: The expired session is removed. The server does not silently replace it with a different ordering under the old token.

steps.title: Explicit refresh creates usable state
steps.note: The new session gets its own lifetime and ordering. The previous cursor remains invalid for its old session.
